candidates.source_name: ЕСЈН — Електронски систем за јавни набавки (e-Nabavki), Public Access portal
candidates.why_relevant: Single mandatory national portal for all public contracts above MKD 500,000. Carries notices (огласи), tender documentation, contract-award notices and realized-contract records for ATM supply/maintenance, POS terminals, card personalisation, cash handling/CIT and core-banking IT bought by state bodies, municipalities, public enterprises and state-owned entities. Directly exposes vendor names, awarded values, quantities and contract durations that vendors never publish.
candidates.access_status: public, free; SPA behind hash routes; anonymous browsing of notices generally allowed, bidding requires registration
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Headless browser (Playwright) against the Angular SPA routes #/notices, #/contracts/0, #/realized-contract and #/dossie/{uuid}/1; capture the underlying JSON XHR endpoints the SPA calls and poll them on a schedule. Filter by CPV codes for ATMs/banking machinery, payment terminals, banking software and security/cash-transport services. WebFetch returned HTTP 403 (bot defence) — treat as bot-defended-but-live, not dead.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from third-party tender aggregators exposing dossie URL pattern

negative_findings.description: Direct WebFetch of the ЕСЈН public access page (https://www.e-nabavki.gov.mk/PublicAccess/Home.aspx) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.
negative_findings.result_summary: No page content retrieved. The site is additionally an Angular single-page app addressed by hash routes, so even a successful plain fetch would return an empty shell. This is a hypothesis of bot defence, NOT evidence the portal is dead — third-party aggregators are actively indexing live dossier URLs from it.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important source in this cell cannot be collected with naive HTTP. Collection design must budget for a headless browser or for reverse-engineering the SPA's JSON XHR endpoints.

negative_findings.description: No specific, currently-live North Macedonian public tender for ATMs, POS terminals or card personalisation was surfaced by open web search in either mk or en.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned the portals and the legal framework but no individual banking-hardware notice. The only ATM/POS tender text retrieved was from an unrelated Ethiopian bank, and 'card personalisation' matched an unrelated company profile.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that item-level tender intelligence in this cell is not reachable through general search engines — it requires querying ЕСЈН directly by CPV code. Absence in search results is not absence of tenders.

negative_findings.description: No State Audit Office report specifically on cash operations of Пошта / the postal savings channel was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: The ДЗР report register was confirmed to exist and be public, but the specific audit was not found via search. The register is filterable and full-text searchable at source, which search engines do not index well.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Postal cash-handling audits would be a high-value read on non-bank cash volumes. This should be re-attempted by crawling the ДЗР register directly rather than by search engine.

brief: North Macedonia's public-procurement disclosure for payment and cash infrastructure funnels through one mandatory hub — ЕСЈН at e-nabavki.gov.mk, which carries notices, tender dossiers, awards and realized contracts for every public contract above MKD 500,000 — ringed by three official layers that add what the hub omits: the Bureau of Public Procurement (БЈН) for methodology and annual volume statistics, the State Audit Office (ДЗР) for operational detail on cash handling and bank fees inside audited entities, and the Appeals Commission (ДКЖЈН) for the losing-bidder and pricing detail that award notices suppress. The highest-value buyers in this cell are the state-owned post (АД Пошта на Северна Македонија), the National Bank as a buyer of cash-processing equipment, the tax authority УЈП (which both procures and licenses fiscal devices), and the utility/transport public enterprises that collect the bulk of the country's retail cash. The principal practical obstacle is technical rather than legal: ЕСЈН is a hash-routed single-page app that returned HTTP 403 to a plain fetch, so collection must run through headless browsing or its underlying JSON endpoints, with Opentender.eu and TED serving as normalised but licence-constrained and partially-covering fallbacks. Everything relevant is in Macedonian; CPV-code filtering rather than keyword search is the reliable way to enumerate ATM, POS, card-personalisation and cash-handling procurement, and that code mapping is the main outstanding piece of work.
